correctness.rationale: For each of the explicitly defined 16-vertex graphs, an ordinary P4 as a possibly chorded subgraph is forbidden; independently enumerated 636 Shrikhande and 620 rook distinct four-vertex obstructions. Independently enumerated all retained faces and reconstructed 3,193 versus 3,305 total counts and reduced Euler 7 versus 55. Examined the exact checker: independent four-vertex order tests, complete face-poset directed-acyclic matching (13,536 versus 14,064 incidences), orientation-correct integral Morse differentials, unimodular Smith reductions with only unit nonzero invariants, plus separate original-simplicial mod-two boundary ranks. Critical counts and boundary ranks imply respectively H3 Z32, H4 Z45, H5 Z6 and H4 Z73, H5 Z18 without torsion. This is a finite complete graph-pair result, not an all-SRG theorem.
residual_risks: Independent replay covered forbidden sets, face counts and Euler checks; the full integral Smith reduction of the repository checker was inspected but not separately executed here.
Homology does not determine full homotopy or an all-strongly-regular classification.

value.rationale: Forbidden ordinary P4 subgraphs form a natural (Taylan) path-devoid simplicial functor. Exact integral groups on the canonical Shrikhande/rook strongly regular pair demonstrate that this non-flag topology detects features invisible to their identical strongly regular parameters; the different invariant is not forced by their known independence wedges. It provides exact finite benchmark data for future techniques and is not an arbitrary graph labeling trick.
residual_risks: The qualitative ability to distinguish these graphs was known by other invariants; value resides in the exact nontrivial P4-devoid groups, not claiming first distinction.
